documented_facts: Agent Registry governs standalone skills as top-level Skill resources.
Standalone skills are distinct from A2A skills, which are declarative metadata blocks represented inline in an agent's Agent Card.
Standalone skills use Skill, SkillRevision, and Publisher API resources.
Administrators can apply fine-grained access policies to registered standalone skills.
SkillRevision resources provide immutable versioned snapshots and version history.
reasonable_inferences: Durable resource identity and revision history can make reusable capabilities easier to inspect and control than instructions retained only in transient model context.

Governed Signal-to-Content operates at a different boundary and additionally governs source identity, evidence lineage, duplicate suppression, deterministic workflow state, approval authority, publication authorization, persistent local state, and append-only receipts.
direct_similarities: Capabilities are treated as managed resources.
Both designs value durable operational identity.
Both designs value revision history, controlled reuse, and lifecycle governance.
broader_industry_trends: Agent infrastructure is moving from transient prompt handling toward managed capabilities with identity, versioning, and explicit governance boundaries.
qualification_reason: Current primary documentation supports substantive novelty and bounded structural overlap without claiming architectural equivalence.
